claims.value: Sołtyk gives side A 14,000 troops ready to take the field around Warsaw under Poniatowski at campaign opening.
claims.rationale: Campaign-opening assembly, not a count of all men engaged at Raszyn. English rendering (ours): "The total troops ready to enter the campaign, assembled under Poniatowski in Warsaw and its environs, formed an effective strength of 14,000 men with 39 guns."

citations.locator: soltyk, printed p. 142, Internet Archive leaf 159; inspected page-image excerpt
citations.quote: Le total des troupes prêtes à entrer en campagne, réunies sous les ordres de Poniatowski à Varsovie et aux environs, formait un effectif de 14,000 hommes avec 39 pièces de canon.

claims.value: Welden gives Ferdinand’s side B corps at the end-March assembly as 30,000 men and 5,000 horses, in 25 battalions and 44 squadrons.
claims.rationale: Men and horses are distinct units; no addition to 35,000 people. Earlier corps population differs from Bodart’s battle figure. Printed table totals 42 squadrons after the detached two; not silently reconciled. English rendering (ours): "The seventh Austrian corps under Archduke Ferdinand d’Este, assembling at the end of March at Krakau, Konskie and Radom, consisted of 25 battalions and 44 squadrons, amounting to 30,000 men and 5,000 horses."

citations.locator: welden, printed p. 313, Internet Archive leaf 337; inspected page-image excerpt
citations.quote: Das 7. österreichische Armeecorps unter dem Erzherzog Ferdinand d’Este, welches sich mit Ende März in Krakau, Konskie und Radom zusammenzog, bestand aus 25 Bataillonen, 44 Escadronen, die sich auf 30.000 Mann und 5000 Pferde beliefen.

claims.value: Sołtyk says Ferdinand ordered Mohr to take Falenty before the main army arrived, with support to follow.
claims.rationale: English rendering (ours): "Without waiting for the main body, he ordered General Mohr to take the Falenty position, reserving to himself its support by the first troops arriving on the battlefield."
